The answer is most likely D, about 75%. This is from memory, not a lookup. As I recall, the World Bank's mid-1990s figures had low-income countries at roughly 55% of world population and lower-middle-income countries at about another 15–20%. The $1230 cutoff doesn't match the Bank's standard thresholds as I remember them, so I'm not fully sure.

CONFIDENCE: 55
